recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not remove or rewrite the standalone care-plan-activity value set as part of FHIR-11357; any future lifecycle cleanup for that terminology artifact should be handled as a separate Patient Care or terminology decision.
issue_request: FHIR-11357 was Published with a Persuasive with Modification resolution for DSTU2 CarePlan. It asked that CarePlan.activity.detail.code stop wrapping the SNOMED procedure hierarchy in http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/care-plan-activity and instead bind to the shared Procedure.code value set at http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/procedure-code; the Procedure.code value set itself was to remain unchanged absent a confirmed SNOMED IP problem.
initial_application: The request was applied by commit 25735dcc63a312d77a995ab0d2d8d0ab2ed7f835, which changed the CarePlanActivityType binding in the CarePlan authoring spreadsheet from valueset-care-plan-activity to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/procedure-code. Later source regeneration and refactoring carried that binding into the current StructureDefinition.
additional_context: CarePlan is active in source/fhir.ini. FHIR-26064 later renamed CarePlan.activity.detail to CarePlan.activity.plannedActivityDetail, so the current element to inspect is CarePlan.activity.plannedActivityDetail.code. The old care-plan-activity value set source remains as a standalone terminology artifact, but current CarePlan binding source no longer points the planned activity code element at that wrapper. No directly relevant Zulip or Confluence evidence was found that conflicts with the Jira, source, and git history.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit was made because source/careplan/structuredefinition-CarePlan.xml already binds CarePlan.activity.plannedActivityDetail.code to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/procedure-code.

related_jiras.note: Renamed CarePlan.activity.detail to CarePlan.activity.plannedActivityDetail, which explains the current element path while preserving the FHIR-11357 binding target.
The FHIR-11357 discussion mentioned a similar value-set-wrapping concern for another CarePlan binding; that issue is separate from this code binding.
